turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Hello, Doctor. Well, I guess what brings me in is... I just can't seem to get past how rough and worn my face and hands look. It really bothers me. Whenever I have to do business in town, I feel like every banker or county person is just staring right at the cracks and the spots and the sagging skin. My wife tells me I'm making a big deal out of nothing, that I just look like a man who's worked outdoors his whole life. But I just can't seem to let it go.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient reports being persistently preoccupied with perceived flaws in his face and hands (cracks, spots, sagging skin) that others view as normal aging or outdoor wear, causing him significant distress.

turns.doctor_question: When you're thinking about how your face and hands look, do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like picking at your skin, examining yourself in mirrors, or comparing how you look to other people?
turns.patient_response: Well, yeah, I do. Especially before I have to leave the farm for something important, like a loan meeting at the bank or setting up a table at the craft fair. I'll catch myself checking the bathroom mirror, and then I'll do it again in the truck mirror. I'll just sit there, turning my hat this way and that, trying to see if it casts a shadow to hide the wrinkles. And I definitely compare myself. I'll look at my hands and then think about the younger hands of the guys we hire on, or the folks in town. Sometimes I get so caught up doing all this that I end up wasting time I really should be spending getting work done around the farm.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient reports repetitive appearance-related behaviors including repeated mirror checking, attempting to camouflage wrinkles with a hat, and mentally comparing their hands to others.

turns.doctor_question: Beyond the worry about your face and hands, do you find yourself frequently worried or anxious about other things in your life, like your health, finances, or how things are going on the farm?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. I mean, farming's always a gamble with the weather and prices, so there's the usual stress there. But I wouldn't say I'm worried sick about it or anything. My health is fine, and we make ends meet alright. It's really just... just the way I look that gets to me. That's the only thing that really eats up my thoughts.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient explicitly denies having generalized or excessive anxiety about everyday domains like health, finances, or farm work.
symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient confirms being preoccupied with their appearance, stating that the way they look is the only thing that consumes their thoughts.
